clue.text: Unattractive person, not hurrying, lost wicket — bowled

indicators.note: lost tells us the wicket goes missing from the word for not hurrying

parts.note: someone not hurrying is going slow
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A dawdling batsman loses his wicket, clean bowled, and is judged an ugly sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes W out of SLOW, leaving SLO. In cricket a batsman out bowled is scored B, and a wicket falling is W.
explanation.definitionFit: A slob is a slovenly, untidy and unappealing person, hence an unattractive one.

clue.text: Star introduction to pleasing year

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Star introduction to pleasing year (7,4)': LEAD-IN + G + LAD + Y needs a word for LAD (boy) that is missing, and the scan is unreadable

clue.text: Child's dreadful experience, catching back of hand in frame

indicators.note: catching means the boy's word holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: a boy's is a child's; the possessive gives the S

indicators.note: back of picks the final letter of the word hand

parts.note: a dreadful experience is hell

explanation.surface: A child suffers a nightmare after getting a smack on the hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts D, the last letter of 'hand', into the boy's word. 'frame' looks like a picture frame; it is the shell of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A body shell is the outer frame of a car, the structure the panels form.

clue.text: Don't stare so much, anyway

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words for the first reading: REGARD (stare) LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Regardless is an adverb meaning in any case, a synonym of anyway; split, it says look at less.

clue.text: Captain for one was first to be hurt

parts.note: captain is an example of a military rank
to have led is to have been first or in front

explanation.surface: A team captain was the first to get injured.
explanation.definitionFit: Rankled means caused lasting resentment, so something that rankled hurt one's feelings.

clue.text: August: examiner needed for religious character of Dostoevsky

parts.note: august means grand and majestic
an inquisitor is one who questions or examines

explanation.surface: A dignified questioner is needed for a role from a Russian novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' looks like the month; it is the adjective meaning grand. The Grand Inquisitor is a tale told in The Brothers Karamazov.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand Inquisitor is the churchman in Ivan's parable in Dostoevsky's novel The Brothers Karamazov.

clue.text: Egyptian officer, a god to women

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
dames are women

explanation.surface: An Egyptian soldier is like a deity to the ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: Radames is the Egyptian captain in Verdi's opera Aida.
explanation.definitionFit: Radames is the Egyptian army commander who loves the heroine in Verdi's opera Aida.

clue.text: Three rights don't entirely make a wrong

definitions.text: Three rights don't entirely make a wrong

parts.words: Three rights don't entirely make a wrong
parts.note: the word for a mistake holds three Rs, the abbreviation for right, but has other letters too, so the three rights do not wholly make it

explanation.surface: A twist on the saying that two wrongs don't make a right.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the usual abbreviation for right; the word for a wrong contains three of them plus two other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, a wrong; its spelling contains three Rs.

clue.text: Cake's' singular shape: it comes to a point

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

parts.words: shape: it comes to a point
parts.note: a cone is a solid shape tapering to a point

explanation.surface: A cake with an unusual pointed form.
explanation.definitionFit: A scone is a small plain cake, often eaten with jam and cream at a British tea.

clue.text: Give back all one's cards together

parts.note: to hand in is to return or give back
a hand is all the cards a player holds

explanation.surface: A card player gives back the whole hand at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand in hand is an idiom meaning closely together, as partners walking holding hands.

clue.text: City brought into existence: nothing moved

indicators.note: moved tells us one letter of the word changes its position

parts.note: something brought into existence is born
nothing is the letter O, shaped like a zero

explanation.surface: A city springs into being from nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing' names the O that 'moved' shifts: BORN becomes BRNO with the O sent to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Brno is the second city of the Czech Republic, an example of a city.

clue.text: Yearbook giving sound of thrush

indicators.note: sound of means the word for the bird is said aloud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: the missel (mistle) thrush is a large European thrush

explanation.surface: An annual publication sounds like a songbird.
explanation.walkthrough: A missal is the Roman Catholic book of the Mass for the whole church year, hence a cheeky 'Yearbook'.
explanation.definitionFit: A missal gives the services for every day of the liturgical year, so it is a book of the year.

clue.text: Creator's less than whole-hearted impulse?

parts.note: demi- is a prefix meaning half, so a half-hearted thing is less than whole
an urge is an impulse

explanation.surface: Someone only half committed to a sudden impulse.
explanation.walkthrough: The demiurge is the creator of the world in Platonic and Gnostic thought.
explanation.definitionFit: In Platonic philosophy the demiurge is the divine craftsman who fashions the world, a maker of all things.

clue.text: Love good food, but I'm dangerous Check tod cooking

indicators.note: cooking suggests the letters are mixed and prepared afresh

explanation.surface: A foodie warns that their cooking is risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' shuffles I'M DANGEROUS. 'Check tod' is OCR debris on the page, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To gourmandise is to indulge a love of good food and eat greedily.

clue.text: Moulding English personality needs backing

indicators.note: backing means the two pieces are read from the end towards the start

parts.note: one's ego is one's self or personality

explanation.surface: An Englishman's character needs support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs backing' turns E + EGO into OGEE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogee is an S-shaped architectural moulding with a double curve.

clue.text: Like Hamlet, depressed, and possibly crackers with it

parts.note: Hamlet is the Prince of Denmark, so he is Danish
to feel blue is to be depressed

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's gloomy prince, in low spirits and perhaps going mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like madness to go with Hamlet; it is the biscuits you eat this blue-veined cheese with.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish Blue is a blue-veined cheese often eaten on crackers, so crackers might come with it.

clue.text: Deer with passion for fodder plant

parts.note: a buck is a male deer
heat is passion, as in the heat of the moment

explanation.surface: An amorous stag goes after his food.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckwheat is a plant grown for grain and as animal fodder.

clue.text: Exhibition hall dispenses sour claret

indicators.note: dispenses suggests the letters are handed out and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A venue serves up a bad, acidic red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispenses' shuffles SOUR CLARET. EARLS COURT is a London exhibition centre, long home to trade shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls Court was a large London exhibition centre, a hall used for shows and fairs.

clue.text: One apple and two fish

parts.note: cod is a fish
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A meal of fruit and a pair of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A codling is a variety of cooking apple, so it is one apple.

clue.text: Drum is a feature of some courts

definitions.meaning: in real tennis, the sloping buttress on the end wall of the court

explanation.walkthrough: Real tennis is the old indoor game played in walled courts such as Hampton Court.
explanation.definitionFit: Tambour means a drum, and in real tennis it is the angled projection on the court wall.

clue.text: Bloc formed around politician

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for around
an MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A political alliance gathers around a parliamentarian.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp is a group sharing a position, as a bloc of allies does in politics.

clue.text: During travels, notice islands

indicators.note: During means one piece sits within the other

parts.note: cycles, as a verb, means travels by bicycle
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: On one's journeys one spots an island group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' puts the notice inside the travels. The Cyclades are a Greek island group in the Aegean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclades are an archipelago in the Aegean Sea, a group of Greek islands.

clue.text: One that's silent about one's demand

indicators.note: about means the silent one goes around the other piece

parts.note: a clam, as in clam up, is a silent person
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is no letter

explanation.surface: A quiet person speaks up about what they want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside CLAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim is a demand for something as one's due.

clue.text: Make no haste to draw line under throat

indicators.note: in a down clue the line sits below the throat, so it follows it

parts.note: the craw is the throat or crop of a bird

explanation.surface: Someone is slow to draw a line under their throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts L after CRAW in this down clue; 'to draw' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To crawl is to move very slowly, so to take one's time and make no haste.

clue.text: Bird's calling me to fly

parts.note: taken as written
to wing is to fly

explanation.surface: A bird calls out to someone to take flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Mewing is the cry of a gull, a bird's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Mewing is the plaintive cry of a gull or kite, so it is the noise a bird makes.

clue.text: Fixture's off

definitions.meaning: a sports match played at the opponents' ground

explanation.definitionFit: An away fixture is a match at the other side's ground, and away also means off, gone.

clue.text: With such an illness, certain I go sick

indicators.note: sick suggests the letters are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is convinced they are about to fall ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' shuffles CERTAIN I GO. An iatrogenic illness is one caused by the doctor treating it.
explanation.definitionFit: Iatrogenic describes a condition brought on by medical treatment, so it qualifies a kind of illness.

clue.text: Graduate waiter? He's not bad, really

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
someone who waits about is a lingerer

explanation.surface: A highly educated waiter turns out to be quite decent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waiter' suggests a restaurant; it is one who waits about. 'not bad, really' means not truly ill, which is the shirker's pretence.
explanation.definitionFit: A malingerer feigns illness to dodge work, so is not really unwell despite claiming to be.

clue.text: One securing rank

definitions.meaning: a person who ties or fastens things
a row or level in a series

explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or level, a rank; read as tie-er it is someone who fastens.
